panel.summary: Hand-rolled trim regex backtracks quadratically (ReDoS) on attacker-controlled note content, replacing upstream's linear `.trim()`
panel.evidence: `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (lines 19-20) is applied at line 134 to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false)` — the full setext-heading paragraph body, i.e. untrusted note text. The first alternative is cheap (`^` without `m` only matches at index 0), but the second, `[ws]+$`, is unanchored at the start: `String.replace` with the `g` flag retries at every offset, and at each offset inside a whitespace run of length k it greedily consumes the rest of the run, fails `$` on the following non-whitespace char, and backtracks one char at a time — O(k) per offset, O(k^2) total. Attack: any workspace member with write access stores content like `x` + `' '.repeat(200000)` + `y\n===` (or the same run on a line above `---`). When a victim opens the note, `NotePreview.render()` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165) calls `md.render()`, `lheading` matches (level set at line 108) and the trim at line 134 burns ~1e10 backtracking steps, hanging the victim's tab — and re-hanging on every subsequent re-render. Upstream markdown-it's `lheading` trims linearly here, so this quadratic path is introduced by the change. Fix: trim by index scan, or use non-global start-anchored matches, or `String.prototype.trim()`.
